thread:
Maya: seeing a weird burst of DNS failures from the eu-west edge provisioner pool — multiple model-fetch pods failing to resolve internal model-storage hostnames, started ~now.
Jun: yep, noticed ~5m ago. kubectl logs show `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` for model-fetch and then long tails of retries.
Kai: quick check: can someone exec into a failing pod and cat /etc/resolv.conf? wondering if ndots or search order got mangled.
Maya: on it — output from pod-xyz: 
```
# cat /etc/resolv.conf
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local eu-west.internal.example.com
nameserver 127.0.0.53
nameserver 10.0.2.10
options ndots:5 timeout:1
```
Jun: node-level /etc/resolv.conf on same host shows a different ordering — DHCP client and kubelet both adding search entries. suspect a concurrent write race where resolvconf hook concatenates lines without proper spacing, length -> truncated search path.
Alde: digging at the forwarder: our node-local-dns (10.0.2.10) logs show lots of SERVFAIL for `model-storage.svc.cluster.local` and then fallback to 127.0.0.53. Looks like split-horizon entries are intermittently missing upstream.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2486 (dns: eu-west edge split-horizon resolution failures impacting model fetch).
Kai: dig from node-local-dns to upstream: `dig @10.0.2.10 model-storage.svc.cluster.local +trace +noall +answer` -> returns nothing, but `dig @10.0.2.10 model-storage.euw.internal +short` works. weird namespace-specific issue.
Maya: i also saw 0 TTL answers from the forwarder right before hits — could be a caching bug where the forwarder returns 0 TTL which evicts client cache immediately, causing thundering repeated upstream queries and saturating egress NAT connections. conntrack on the egress gateway is near limits.
Jun: that would explain the simultaneous provisioning failures we saw: model fetch retries tie up connectors and delay GPU assignment, pushing jobs into backoff and then failing SLOs.
Kai: run these on affected node: 
```
systemctl status systemd-resolved
journalctl -u node-local-dns -n 200 | tail -n 50
ss -n state established sport = :53
sudo conntrack -S | grep udp
```
Maya: pasted node-local-dns tail: `forwarder: upstream returned rcode=0 ttl=0 for model-storage.svc.cluster.local, caching disabled` then `resolver: cache miss, forwarding to 10.10.0.5` (10.10.0.5 is our split-horizon authoritative in that region).
Alde: i pulled tcpdump — see a burst of identical A queries but with different EDNS padding, some responses arriving truncated (TC=1) and our forwarder falling back to TCP which times out under load. Something is corrupting the EDNS buffer occasionally.
Jun: could be MTU/path-mtu issue on the egress NAT path combined with larger EDNS size. We did push a network ACL change yesterday.
Kai: quick mitigation: reduce EDNS size on node-local-dns and set `max-udp-size 512` temporarily; also adjust conntrack to allow higher ephemeral UDP flows and enable `nf_conntrack_max=2000000` on the gateway.
Maya: rolling those out to the three eu-west edge gateways now to test. will also push a small resolvconf hook change to avoid collapsing `search` lines — keep each search on its own line so ndots semantics don't flip.
Alde: we should also pin `options ndots:2` for model fetchers — they expect short search order. forcing ndots:2 in the pod DNSPolicy or via resolv config would avoid the split-horizon going to public resolvers first.
Jun: +1 on ndots tweak for the modelfetch DaemonSet; will submit a patch.
ops-bot: Deploy job queued: config-change/eu-west-edgedns/adjust-edns-512 (ci-runner #4823).
Kai: after mitigation, one node shows reduced SERVFAIL and model-fetch success rate up from 73% -> 98% for new attempts. still monitoring.
Maya: next steps: 1) keep EDNS size cap on forwarders for 24h, 2) revert recent ACL change if degradation recurs, 3) land resolvconf hook patch and rollout, 4) pin ndots for modelfetch pods and schedule a rolling restart.
Jun: leaving an action item to increase conntrack on gateways and add alert if UDP conntrack > 80%.
Alde: adding a follow-up to run an egress MTU check on the path and validate tcpdump for TCP fallback frequency.
Kai: thanks all — will keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks. if anyone sees new fails paste `kubectl get po -n modelfetch -o wide` and we’ll triage.
